# Terminal corpus

`<name>.vt` contains raw PTY output, including the kernel echo of typed input.
`<name>.toml` records the dimensions, scrollback, description and source. Optional
`[[ops]]` entries write byte ranges, resize, scroll, or capture intermediate dumps.
Without operations the test writes the whole stream and captures one dump.

Run `cargo test --features terminal --test widget_behavior_suite terminal_corpus`.
After reviewing an intentional Alacritty change, regenerate the goldens with
`TUI_LIPAN_BLESS_TERMINAL_CORPUS=1` and the same command.

The JSON dumps retain size, history, cursor, modes, replies, semantic state and
cell data. Rows omit default styles and trailing default blank rows. Their `text`
omits trailing spaces; size and style ranges preserve their positions. `cells`
records column/string pairs only for cells containing zero or multiple Unicode
scalars; other cells are single characters from `text`. `styles` records only
non-default style ranges, and `links` and `wrapped` appear only when set.
These omissions cannot hide a changed non-default cell, style, link or wrap flag.

Chunk tests use seeded byte splits. An engine-scoped `[[known_defects]]` entry
names one check, seed, text path and expected/actual substring pair. Additional
`[[known_defects.differences]]` entries must match exact JSON path/value pairs.
The harness rejects stale defects and any other difference. The VTE split-UTF-8
lost-space defect includes its resulting cursor-column change.

`scripts/capture-terminal-corpus` records the real-program fixtures in a neutral
home, checks for personal data, and replaces host hardware details with fixed-width
placeholders. Run it with `--check` to validate the checked-in streams; regeneration
requires the named programs. Time-dependent captures do not reproduce byte for byte.
Handwritten protocol fixtures are not regenerated by the recorder.

The two `long-lines` sizes intentionally share bytes to check different wrap
boundaries. Other identical-stream size twins were omitted; colored bash and ls
captures at two sizes contain different program output.
